body.cap: Kieun Jeon, CEO of Turbine Crew, poses with the CES 2026 Innovation Awards trophy and the ‘ECO-CLEBINE’ catalog. As an exhibitor in the Jeonnam Pavilion, Turbine Crew drew attention on-site by unveiling its renewable energy–based autonomous operation platform. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: At CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition, Turbine Crew (CEO Kieun Jeon), an exhibitor in the Jeonnam Pavilion, attracted attention by presenting a new direction for “energy infrastructure that operates without human presence.” The company was honored with a CES 2026 Innovation Award for its integrated operational model that combines smart turbines with an AI-based platform powered by renewable energy.

At the Turbine Crew booth in the Jeonnam Pavilion at The Venetian Expo in Las Vegas, visitors were introduced to a connected system featuring the small wind turbine ‘ECO-CLEBINE,’ solar power modules, and a renewable energy–powered Drone Station. These components are integrated and managed through Turbine Crew’s smart farm platform, TlatFarm, demonstrating an “operational energy cycle” that connects energy generation, storage, transfer, and drone operations in real time.

“Our focus at CES was not on showcasing individual power-generation devices, but on visualizing a complete cycle—how energy is produced, managed, and ultimately applied to real-world operations,” said Jeon. “The CES Innovation Award is a recognition of this entire structure, encompassing energy, data, and autonomous drone operations, rather than a single product.”
“Connecting Sun, Wind, and Sea”… Autonomous Operations Powered by TlatFarm

Turbine Crew’s core competitive edge lies in TlatFarm Technology. The platform collects and analyzes real-time data from renewable energy facilities such as wind and solar systems, optimizing energy usage while supporting automated drone routing and mission execution. This enables unmanned operation of sites where continuous human presence is difficult, including farmland monitoring, coastal facility inspections, and renewable energy asset maintenance.

Jeonnam Province provides an ideal environment for such a model. With its expansive agricultural plains, strong farming base, long coastline, and steady sea winds, the region offers favorable conditions for testing distributed renewable energy and drone-based management technologies. Turbine Crew designed its platform around these characteristics, integrating solar power, the small wind turbine ECO-CLEBINE, and coastal-ready structures into a single operational system.
"Designing a Landscape, Not Just a Machine: The ECO-CLEBINE Approach"

One of the most eye-catching products at the booth was the small wind turbine ECO-CLEBINE. Designed to operate at wind speeds as low as 2 meters per second, the turbine features a low-noise structure and a 360-degree omnidirectional rotation system, allowing it to respond flexibly to changing wind directions and intensities.

body.cap: Overview of the Jeonnam Pavilion at CES 2026. The joint pavilion organized by Jeollanam-do and Jeonnam Technopark brings together innovative Korean technology companies, drawing continuous interest from global buyers and visitors. | Photo – AVING News

body.x: Its exterior design clearly differentiates it from conventional industrial wind equipment. By adopting curved forms and a restrained aesthetic, ECO-CLEBINE was created to harmonize with rural landscapes and coastal environments. Jeon emphasized that “the wind turbine was designed not simply as a power-generation machine, but as part of a space where nature and people coexist,” adding that “design is not merely aesthetic—it is a strategic element that enhances technological acceptance.”

Jeon’s background reflects this philosophy. With prior experience at wind-related companies and at Kolon Global, combined with academic training in architectural design, environmental engineering, and land-use studies, he has applied a multidisciplinary perspective to Turbine Crew’s product and platform development. This integrated understanding of structure, environment, and design has shaped the company’s current technology.

Turbine Crew is headquartered in Naju, Jeonnam, and also operates a U.S. subsidiary. According to Jeon, the company’s goal is to expand the energy cycle validated in Jeonnam’s sea and plains into global markets spanning agriculture, urban infrastructure, and renewable energy systems.

By clearly imprinting the concept of “operational energy” on the CES 2026 exhibition floor, Turbine Crew demonstrated how technologies born from regional environments can evolve into globally scalable standards.
